subject: Finalize audit-rights & evidence handoff for MSA / Order Form (Lumina Diagnostics)
messages:
From: Evan Bell <evan.bell@lumina-dx.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lumina-dx.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft OF/MSA redlines — SOC2 coverage + pen-test window

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier. We have Lumina’s procurement and security team reviewing the MSA + Order Form and have a few open items we need to resolve before legal will sign: primarily the security exhibit / audit rights language and how evidence will be handed off (SOC 2, pen testing).

Can you confirm the following:
- Which SOC 2 coverage Redwood will provide (Type II attestation — last 12 months, and whether the report can be shared with NDA).
- A pen-test cadence you typically accept (annual vs. biannual) and whether Lumina can engage an external firm with regional IP scanning rules.
- Scope boundaries: we need to limit audit rights to the infrastructure supporting Lumina’s production tenant(s).
- Evidence cadence: procurement wants a quarterly or on-demand evidence path (logs, configuration snapshots) and a secure delivery mechanism.

I attached our current draft of the redlined Order Form so you can see the language that triggered questions. Our target is to finalize this by next week so CFO can sign.

Thanks — please loop in legal/security at Redwood if needed.

Best,
Evan Bell
Chief Procurement Officer
Lumina Diagnostics
Attachment: lumina_draft_orderform_redlines.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Bell <evan.bell@lumina-dx.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft OF/MSA redlines — SOC2 coverage + pen-test window

Evan — thanks for the clear list. High level answers and proposed path forward below. Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to walk through.

Summary (proposed):
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II (covering the most recent 12-month period). We can share the full report under a standard NDA/attestation process and via a secured Drive link (see related link).
- Pen test: Redwood conducts annual third-party penetration testing. For customers that require on-site or customer-engaged tests we accept coordinated external vendors; we ask that tests be scoped to production infrastructure that directly supports the customer’s tenancy and that IP ranges and test types be pre-approved.
- Audit rights & scope: We will accept audit rights restricted to systems supporting Lumina production workloads. We propose a defined scope appendix in the security exhibit listing services, regions, and allowed data types.
- Evidence cadence: Quarterly push of evidence artifacts (SOC 2 report, summary of pen-test findings, relevant audit logs) via a secure link; ad-hoc evidence requests will require a 7-day notice so we can collect and sanitize artifacts.

Proposed contractual language (snippet for the security exhibit):
- "Redwood shall provide Customer with Redwood’s most recent SOC 2 Type II report upon execution of an appropriate NDA; scheduled penetration testing results and a summary of remediations will be made available on a quarterly cadence or upon 7 days' notice for validated audit requests. Audit rights are limited to systems and infrastructure used to serve Customer’s production tenancy as specified in Appendix A."

Next steps:
1) I attached a short draft of a security exhibit (proposed_security_exhibit_v1.docx) with the appendix placeholder for Scope.
2) If Lumina’s legal wants additional access (on-site auditors or expanded forensic access) please flag and we’ll route to Exec Legal — that will likely need cost-recovery and more narrow timing.
3) Karthik / Neha: can you review the snippet and the appendix scope in the attached and flag anything Redwood legal/security will not accept?

Thanks — I’ll aim to turn around redlines same day after your comments.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_security_exhibit_v1.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evan Bell <evan.bell@lumina-dx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft OF/MSA redlines — SOC2 coverage + pen-test window

Evan / Lauren — quick legal / compliance read-through below. I’m copying Marissa (legal) and Neha (security) for detailed redlines.

Legal notes (high level):
- Agree with restricting audit rights to production tenancy. Please ensure Appendix A includes explicit service identifiers (model-serving, KV cache, auth gateway) and region tags.
- Evidence requests: we can commit to a 7-day lead time for most requests. For unusually broad requests (e.g., forensic-level exports or cross-tenant logs) we need a written scope and may require a separate executed data-access addendum.
- Pen testing: Redwood will accept customer-engaged third-party tests provided they sign our tester NDA and follow approved scope/IP lists. We cannot accept uncontrolled brute-force or broad internet-wide scanning.
- On-site auditors: remove any requirement for unlimited on-site access. We can accommodate up to 2 auditors on-site for a single 3-day window with prior notice and cost-recovery for facilities/support if requested.

Operational asks from Security (Neha):
- Please specify allowed test classes (OWASP top 10, authenticated API tests) and explicitly exclude infrastructure-layer DDoS or noise-generating tests.
- Provide Lumina the contact for scheduling and IP allowlists. We’ll publish a standard tester onboarding form.

I’ve attached legal redlines (legal_redlines_marked.pdf) with tracked suggestions and a short comment on the cost-recovery clause. Lauren — please incorporate or push back where necessary.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: legal_redlines_marked.pdf
